periodic square cellulation has vertices $q_{i,j}$, horizontal edges $h_{i,j}$
from $q_{i,j}$ to $q_{i+1,j}$, vertical edges $v_{i,j}$ from $q_{i,j}$ to
$q_{i,j+1}$, and faces $f_{i,j}$, for $i,j\in\mathbb Z_L$. Every index is
read modulo $L$. The boundary of $f_{i,j}$ consists of
$h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},h_{i,j+1},v_{i,j}$. Equivalently, this is the quotient of
the unit square tiling of $\mathbb R^2$ by translations in $L\mathbb Z^2$.

The cellulation has $L^2$ vertices, $2L^2$ edges, and $L^2$ faces. The
condition $L\ge3$ ensures that the four edges in each star and face are
distinct, and that every edge has two distinct endpoints and two distinct
incident faces. The vertex-edge graph joins vertices joined by an edge. The
face-adjacency graph joins faces sharing an edge; both graphs are connected.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

$$E g_j=(-1)^{s_j(E)}g_jE,\qquad s_j(E):=\omega(\lambda(E),\lambda(g_j)).$$

The **logical Pauli classes** form the quotient group

$$N(S)/(Z_nS).$$

A normalizer element is logically nontrivial exactly when it lies in
$N(S)\setminus Z_nS$. Multiplication by a scalar phase does not change a
syndrome or logical class.

derivations.claim: The primal vertex-edge graph has the explicit spanning tree $T=\{h_{i,0}:0\le i<L-1\}\cup\{v_{i,j}:i\in\mathbb Z_L,\ 0\le j<L-1\}$. The horizontal edges form a path through row zero, and each other row is attached to that path by one vertical column path; hence $T$ is connected and has no cycle. For each edge $e\notin T$, add $e$ to the unique tree path between its endpoints. This gives a cycle $\gamma_e$ containing $e$ and no other edge outside $T$. These cycles are independent because the coefficient of each non-tree edge in a linear combination is its own coefficient. They span $Z_1$: subtract from any cycle the $\gamma_e$ corresponding to its non-tree edges; the remainder is an even-incidence chain supported on the tree, and a nonempty finite forest has a leaf of odd degree, so the remainder is zero. Thus $\dim Z_1=|E|-(|V|-1)=L^2+1$.

Every face boundary has even incidence at each vertex, so $B_1\subseteq Z_1$. By [F2], $\dim B_1=L^2-1$. For a cycle $c$, define $w_h^k(c)=\sum_j c(h_{k,j})$ and $w_v^\ell(c)=\sum_i c(v_{i,\ell})$, with all sums in $\mathbb F_2$. Summing the even-incidence equations over column $k$ shows $w_h^k=w_h^{k-1}$; summing over row $\ell$ shows $w_v^\ell=w_v^{\ell-1}$. Thus the two parities $w_h,w_v$ are independent of the chosen cuts. Each face boundary crosses every such cut zero or two times, so both parities vanish on $B_1$.

The horizontal fundamental loop $\gamma_h=\sum_i h_{i,0}$ has $(w_h,w_v)=(1,0)$, and the vertical fundamental loop $\gamma_v=\sum_j v_{0,j}$ has $(w_h,w_v)=(0,1)$. Therefore no nonzero combination of these loops lies in $B_1$. A basis of $B_1$ together with $\gamma_h,\gamma_v$ is an independent family of $(L^2-1)+2=L^2+1$ cycles, which is the dimension of $Z_1$ from step 1.1. $$\mathcal C(S):=\{\psi\in(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}:g\psi=\psi\text{ for every }g\in S\}.$$

stabilizer rank is $r$; independence means no nonempty product of distinct
generators is $I$. The code-space projector and its nonzero dimension are
established by [[thm-qc-stabilizer-projector-and-dimension]].

$$P_S:=|S|^{-1}\sum_{g\in S}g$$

On the periodic torus, define four Pauli representatives

$$\bar Z_1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{h_{i,0}},\qquad \bar Z_2=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{v_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_1=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{h_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_2=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{v_{i,0}}.$$

The $\bar Z$ supports are the two fixed fundamental primal cycles. The
$\bar X$ supports are the dual cycles crossing them. These operators are
called the toric logical loops. As verified below, each is a nontrivial
logical Pauli class in the periodic toric code.

For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup generated by an ordered independent
Hermitian list $g_1,\ldots,g_r$. For a phase-aware Pauli error $E$, its
**syndrome** is the bit string $s(E)\in\mathbb F_2^r$ defined by

$$E g_j=(-1)^{s_j(E)}g_jE,\qquad s_j(E):=\omega(\lambda(E),\lambda(g_j)).$$

Here $\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$ is the binary Pauli label and
$\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'$. The scalar center of
$\mathcal P_n$ is $Z_n=\{i^kI:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$, and the
**normalizer** is $N(S)=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:Pg=gP\text{ for every }g\in S\}$.
The **logical Pauli classes** form the quotient group

$$N(S)/(Z_nS).$$

A normalizer element is logically nontrivial exactly when it lies in
$N(S)\setminus Z_nS$. Multiplication by a scalar phase does not change a
syndrome or logical class.

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric checks with $L\ge3$, the common $+1$
eigenspace is a valid stabilizer code on $n=2L^2$ qubits. Its independent
check rank is $r=2L^2-2$, so its dimension is
$2^{n-r}=4=2^2$ and it encodes two logical qubits.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be an $n$-qubit stabilizer group generated by $r$ independent
commuting Hermitian Pauli checks with $-I\notin S$. Then the logical Pauli
quotient $N(S)/(Z_nS)$ is a binary vector space of dimension $2(n-r)$.
Consequently, it is nontrivial exactly when the stabilizer code encodes at
least one qubit.

Let $P$ be a primal path and $Q$ a dual path whose edge supports share
exactly one physical qubit. Then their string Paulis anticommute:
$Z(P)X(Q)=-X(Q)Z(P)$. This is the algebraic mutual e/m string sign.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $\bar Z_1$ and $\bar X_1$ share only $h_{0,0}$, while $\bar Z_2$ and $\bar X_2$ share only $v_{0,0}$. [F6] gives anticommutation for these equal-index pairs. Suppose a product $\bar Z_1^a\bar Z_2^b\bar X_1^c\bar X_2^d$, with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb F_2$, represented the identity class in [F3]. It would then commute with every normalizer representative. By [F4] the code has $k=2$, and [F5] gives logical quotient dimension $2k=4$. The four independent classes from step 2.1 therefore form a basis of that quotient.

Fix $L\ge3$, $J_e,J_m>0$, a unit vector $\psi$ in the toric code space, and
a specified nontrivial logical Pauli representative $Q$. An **elementary
Pauli path to $Q$** is a finite sequence $E_0,\ldots,E_T$ with $E_0=I$,
$E_T$ a scalar-phase multiple of $Q$, and
$E_{r+1}=P_rE_r$, where each $P_r$ is $X$, $Y$, or $Z$ on a single edge and
the identity on every other edge.

For any prefix Pauli $E$, define its energy excess
$\varepsilon(E):=\langle E\psi,H_LE\psi\rangle-E_{\rm code}$, where
$E_{\rm code}:=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$ is the energy of every code vector. The
**Pauli-path energy barrier** of $Q$ is

$$\mathcal B_L(Q):=\min_{(E_0,\ldots,E_T)}\max_{0\le r\le T}\varepsilon(E_r),$$

where the minimum ranges over elementary Pauli paths to $Q$. This is a
finite-code energy quantity; it is not a thermal lifetime.

For the finite toric-code Hamiltonian
$H_L=-J_e\sum_q A_q-J_m\sum_f B_f$ with $J_e,J_m>0$, the ground space is
the four-dimensional toric code space and the ground energy is
$E_g=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$. The exact spectral gap above it is
$\Delta_L=4\min(J_e,J_m)$.

Let $P$ be a primal edge trail with no repeated edge and distinct endpoints
$q_0,q_1$. The Pauli string $Z(P)$ has commutation syndrome $1$ at exactly
the two endpoint stars and $0$ at every other star or plaquette. Let $Q$ be
a dual edge trail with no repeated edge and distinct endpoint faces
$f_0,f_1$. The string $X(Q)$ has commutation syndrome $1$ at exactly those
two endpoint plaquettes and $0$ at every other plaquette or star.

If either kind of edge-simple trail is closed, its corresponding string has
zero syndrome at every check.

On the periodic torus, define four Pauli representatives

$$\bar Z_1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{h_{i,0}},\qquad \bar Z_2=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{v_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_1=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{h_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_2=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{v_{i,0}}.$$

The $\bar Z$ supports are the two fixed fundamental primal cycles. The
$\bar X$ supports are the dual cycles crossing them. These operators are
called the toric logical loops. As verified below, each is a nontrivial
logical Pauli class in the periodic toric code.

For $L\ge3$ and couplings $J_e,J_m>0$, the finite toric-code Hamiltonian on
$\mathcal H_L$ is

$$H_L=-J_e\sum_{i,j\in\mathbb Z_L}A_{i,j}-J_m\sum_{i,j\in\mathbb Z_L}B_{i,j}.$$

The energy unit is fixed by $J_e,J_m$. This is a finite-volume operator
defined from the stabilizer checks; its definition makes no claim about a
material realization or a thermodynamic phase.

derivations.claim: Suppose $J_e\le J_m$. Apply $Z_{h_{0,0}},Z_{h_{1,0}},\ldots,Z_{h_{L-1,0}}$ in that order. After $k$ factors with $1\le k<L$, the partial string is a primal trail from $q_{0,0}$ to $q_{k,0}$; these endpoints are distinct, so [F3] gives exactly two e defects and no m defects. By [F5], changing one star eigenvalue from $+1$ to $-1$ changes its energy contribution from $-J_e$ to $+J_e$, an increase of $2J_e$; the excess is therefore $4J_e$. After the last factor the path is closed and has zero syndrome by [F3]. This is an elementary path in [F1] whose peak excess is at most $4J_e$.

Suppose $J_m<J_e$. Apply $X_{v_{0,0}},X_{v_{1,0}},\ldots,X_{v_{L-1,0}}$ in that order. The crossed dual edges form a closed horizontal dual loop. After $k$ factors with $1\le k<L$, the dual trail has distinct endpoint faces $f_{L-1,0}$ and $f_{k-1,0}$; [F3] gives exactly two m defects and no e defects. By [F5], each m defect raises the energy by $2J_m$, so the excess is $4J_m$. The final closed trail has zero syndrome by [F3] and ends at $\bar X_2$. This is an elementary path in [F1] with peak excess at most $4J_m$.
If $J_e\le J_m$, step 1.1 gives $4J_e=4\min(J_e,J_m)$. If $J_m<J_e$, step 1.2 gives $4J_m=4\min(J_e,J_m)$. The bound is independent of $L$.

code projector. Let $D$ be a compact embedded disk in the torus with
connected complement. Let $S\subseteq E_L$ be a set of edge qubits such that

noncontractible logical loop of the cheaper species has barrier at most

check rank is $r=2L^2-2$, so its dimension is

derivations.claim: Since [F1] identifies the code as the ground eigenspace of the self-adjoint finite operator [F5], its orthogonal projector $\Pi_L$ commutes with $H_L$: for $\psi$ in the code and $\eta\perp\mathcal C$, $\langle\psi,H_L\eta\rangle=\langle H_L\psi,\eta\rangle =E_g\langle\psi,\eta\rangle=0$. The complement is nonzero by [F4], so the restriction of $H_L$ to it has a least eigenvalue. By [F1] that eigenvalue is $E_g+\Delta_L$. The other finite-volume properties [F2] and [F3] concern this same unperturbed Hamiltonian and code.

Define $V_L=-\Delta_L(I-\Pi_L)$. The operator $I-\Pi_L$ is a nonzero orthogonal projection by [F4], so $V_L$ is self-adjoint and $\|V_L\|=\Delta_L$. It vanishes on the code and subtracts $\Delta_L$ from every eigenvalue on the orthogonal complement. The construction uses the global code projector and is not asserted to belong to a local perturbation class.

The code eigenvalue remains $E_g$ after adding $V_L$. Every excited eigenvalue $E\ge E_g+\Delta_L$ becomes $E-\Delta_L\ge E_g$, and a nonzero eigenspace with $E=E_g+\Delta_L$ now also has eigenvalue $E_g$. Fix an integer $L\ge3$ and write $\mathbb Z_L=\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$. The
periodic square cellulation has vertices $q_{i,j}$, horizontal edges $h_{i,j}$
from $q_{i,j}$ to $q_{i+1,j}$, vertical edges $v_{i,j}$ from $q_{i,j}$ to
$q_{i,j+1}$, and faces $f_{i,j}$, for $i,j\in\mathbb Z_L$. Every index is
read modulo $L$. The boundary of $f_{i,j}$ consists of
$h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},h_{i,j+1},v_{i,j}$. Equivalently, this is the quotient of
the unit square tiling of $\mathbb R^2$ by translations in $L\mathbb Z^2$.

The cellulation has $L^2$ vertices, $2L^2$ edges, and $L^2$ faces. The
condition $L\ge3$ ensures that the four edges in each star and face are
distinct, and that every edge has two distinct endpoints and two distinct
incident faces. The vertex-edge graph joins vertices joined by an edge. The
face-adjacency graph joins faces sharing an edge; both graphs are connected.

For the periodic cellulation in [[def-qc-tqc-periodic-square-cellulation]],
put one qubit on each edge, ordered lexicographically by $(i,j)$ and then with
horizontal before vertical edges. The physical Hilbert space is
$\mathcal H_L=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes E}$, where $E$ is the edge set. For an
edge $e$, write $X_e$ and $Z_e$ for the corresponding one-qubit Pauli acting
on that tensor factor and as the identity on every other factor. Define the
star and plaquette checks by

$$A_{i,j}=X_{h_{i-1,j}}X_{h_{i,j}}X_{v_{i,j-1}}X_{v_{i,j}},\qquad B_{i,j}=Z_{h_{i,j}}Z_{v_{i+1,j}}Z_{h_{i,j+1}}Z_{v_{i,j}}.$$

All indices are in $\mathbb Z_L$.

All star and plaquette checks of [[def-qc-tqc-toric-checks]] commute. The
product of all stars is the identity, and the product of all plaquettes is
the identity.

For $L\ge3$, the $L^2$ star-support vectors in $\mathbb F_2^E$ have span
dimension $L^2-1$, and their only relation is their total sum. The $L^2$
face-boundary vectors have the same span dimension and their only relation
is their total sum. The dual-face incidence statement has the same rank.

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric checks with $L\ge3$, the common $+1$
eigenspace is a valid stabilizer code on $n=2L^2$ qubits. Its independent
check rank is $r=2L^2-2$, so its dimension is
$2^{n-r}=4=2^2$ and it encodes two logical qubits.

On the periodic torus, define four Pauli representatives

$$\bar Z_1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{h_{i,0}},\qquad \bar Z_2=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{v_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_1=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{h_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_2=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{v_{i,0}}.$$

The $\bar Z$ supports are the two fixed fundamental primal cycles. The
$\bar X$ supports are the dual cycles crossing them. These operators are
called the toric logical loops. As verified below, each is a nontrivial
logical Pauli class in the periodic toric code.

Let $P$ be a primal edge trail with no repeated edge and distinct endpoints
$q_0,q_1$. The Pauli string $Z(P)$ has commutation syndrome $1$ at exactly
the two endpoint stars and $0$ at every other star or plaquette. Let $Q$ be
a dual edge trail with no repeated edge and distinct endpoint faces
$f_0,f_1$. The string $X(Q)$ has commutation syndrome $1$ at exactly those
two endpoint plaquettes and $0$ at every other plaquette or star.

If either kind of edge-simple trail is closed, its corresponding string has
zero syndrome at every check.

For the finite toric-code Hamiltonian
$H_L=-J_e\sum_q A_q-J_m\sum_f B_f$ with $J_e,J_m>0$, the ground space is
the four-dimensional toric code space and the ground energy is
$E_g=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$. The exact spectral gap above it is
$\Delta_L=4\min(J_e,J_m)$.

For $L\ge3$ and couplings $J_e,J_m>0$, the finite toric-code Hamiltonian on
$\mathcal H_L$ is

$$H_L=-J_e\sum_{i,j\in\mathbb Z_L}A_{i,j}-J_m\sum_{i,j\in\mathbb Z_L}B_{i,j}.$$

The energy unit is fixed by $J_e,J_m$. This is a finite-volume operator
defined from the stabilizer checks; its definition makes no claim about a
material realization or a thermodynamic phase.

Delete the star $A_{0,0}$ and plaquette $B_{0,0}$ from the full check list,
and call the remaining $r=2L^2-2$ checks $g_1,\ldots,g_r$. They are
independent commuting Hermitian involutions. For each sign string
$s\in\mathbb F_2^r$, the operator

$$P_s=\prod_{a=1}^r\frac{I+(-1)^{s_a}g_a}{2}$$

is the orthogonal projection onto the corresponding joint eigenspace; the
$P_s$ are pairwise orthogonal and sum to the identity. The omitted checks
are determined by the retained ones, so every nonzero syndrome sector has
an even number of e defects and an even number of m defects.

For a nonzero vector $\psi$ that is a simultaneous eigenvector of all toric
checks, its **e syndrome** is the set of vertices $q$ for which
$A_q\psi=-\psi$, and its **m syndrome** is the set of faces $f$ for which
$B_f\psi=-\psi$. A violated star is called an e defect and a violated
plaquette is called an m defect. These are finite stabilizer-syndrome labels;
the names do not assume that a material contains localized physical
quasiparticles.

The word **syndrome** follows the check-eigenvalue convention of
[[def-qc-stabilizer-syndrome-and-logical-operators]].

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Take the square grid with vertices $(i,j)$ for
$0\le i,j\le d$, unit horizontal and vertical edges, and $d^2$ square faces.
Let $R$ consist of the left and right vertical boundary edges together with
their vertices. The physical qubits are the edges not in $R$; there are
$2d^2$ such edges. Order vertices and faces lexicographically by their
coordinates, and order physical edges lexicographically by their lower
endpoint, with horizontal edges before vertical edges when endpoints tie.

Let $Q_0$ be the binary vector space on vertices outside $R$, $Q_1$ the
binary vector space on physical edges, and $Q_2$ the binary vector space on
faces. Define $\partial_1:Q_1\to Q_0$ by sending each physical edge to the
sum of its endpoints that are outside $R$. Define $\partial_2:Q_2\to Q_1$
by sending each face to its boundary with any edge in $R$ deleted.

The X-check matrix is $H_X=\partial_1$, with rows indexed by vertices
outside $R$ and columns by physical edges. The Z-check matrix is
$H_Z=\partial_2^{\mathsf T}$, with rows indexed by faces and columns by
physical edges. Thus X checks are the rows of $H_X$ and Z checks are the
rows of $H_Z$. The maps satisfy $\partial_1\partial_2=0$. The rough
boundaries are the left and right sides; the top and bottom are the
complementary dual boundaries.

For the relative $d\times d$ square patch of
[[def-qc-square-planar-surface-code]], the code encodes one logical qubit and
has stabilizer distance $d$. Every nontrivial Z logical class contains a
rough-to-rough path of length at least $d$, and a straight row attains $d$.
Every nontrivial X logical class contains a top-to-bottom dual path of length
at least $d+1$. For each $\ell\ge1$, the number of self-avoiding
rough-to-rough paths of length $\ell$ is at most $(d+1)3^\ell$.

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric stabilizer code with $L\ge3$, the
minimum weight of a normalizer Pauli outside the scalar-phase stabilizer is
$d(S)=L$.

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric checks with $L\ge3$, the common $+1$
eigenspace is a valid stabilizer code on $n=2L^2$ qubits. Its independent
check rank is $r=2L^2-2$, so its dimension is
$2^{n-r}=4=2^2$ and it encodes two logical qubits.

On the periodic torus, define four Pauli representatives

$$\bar Z_1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{h_{i,0}},\qquad \bar Z_2=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{v_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_1=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{h_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_2=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{v_{i,0}}.$$

The $\bar Z$ supports are the two fixed fundamental primal cycles. The
$\bar X$ supports are the dual cycles crossing them. These operators are
called the toric logical loops. As verified below, each is a nontrivial
logical Pauli class in the periodic toric code.

derivations.claim: Set $d=L=3$. By [F2], the planar code has Z distance $3$ and X distance $4$, and encodes one qubit. For the toric code, [F3] gives the lower bound $3$ for every nontrivial logical Pauli, while [F5] supplies a nontrivial three-edge representative of each pure species. Thus both species have distance $3$; [F4] gives code dimension four. The distance profiles and code dimensions differ at the same linear size.

The reason is already present in the hypotheses: [F1] uses relative boundary maps and rough edges, while [F3] uses periodic incidence on a closed torus. Therefore planar boundary paths and their asymmetric distance theorem do not establish torus winding classes, check relations, or toric distance. The distinction is a finite combinatorial one and does not require a physical interpretation.
